title: MO-IPS suppresses acute myeloid leukemia through metabolic reprogramming and synergizes with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy.
authors: Wang, Yingwen; Zhao, Wenjun; Jin, Yanrui; Hu, Chen; Fang, Xingqi; Dong, Shuhong; Zhang, Baolai
one_liner_zh: 该文研究MO-IPS抑制剂对急性髓系白血病的代谢重编程及免疫协同作用，仅涉及分子对接预测药物结合靶点，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Our prior research identified MO-IPS as a potent MYC-PRMT inhibitor. Here, we re-evaluated its efficacy at optimized lower doses to explore a wider therapeutic window. MO-IPS retained robust anti-proliferative activity in vitro at reduced exposures. In MV-4-11 xenografts, the higher established dose suppressed tumor growth by 72.3% and enabled metabolomic profiling. This revealed a sequential mechanism: rapid MYC suppression followed by delayed downregulation of metabolic enzymes, inducing concurrent disruption of heme biosynthesis and NAD(+) metabolism. Molecular docking predicted potential binding to UPP1, GAMT, and IDO2, and we observed that MO-IPS downregulates their expression at mRNA and protein levels. Critically, in an immunocompetent C1498 model, a lower, therapeutically relevant dose of MO-IPS (20 mg/kg), titrated to minimize direct cytotoxicity, synergized with PD-1 therapy achieving 68.1% tumor inhibition. Mechanistically, the combination enhanced CD8(+) T cell infiltration and reduced Treg accumulation, leading to an elevated CD8/Foxp3 ratio. This pivotal finding demonstrates that at reduced exposure, MO-IPS's anti-leukemic efficacy is driven not by overt cytotoxicity but by metabolic reprogramming that establishes a pro-immunogenic tumor microenvironment. Collectively, our work repositions MO-IPS from a cytotoxic MYC-PRMT inhibitor to a multifaceted immunometabolic therapeutic. At optimized lower doses, it orchestrates a coordinated disruption of cancer metabolic vulnerabilities and actively augments anti-tumor immunity, presenting a refined and highly promising combinatorial strategy for AML.
abstract_zh: 我们先前的研究确定MO-IPS为一种强效的MYC-PRMT抑制剂。在此，我们在优化后的较低剂量下重新评估其疗效，以探索更宽的治疗窗口。在减少暴露量下，MO-IPS在体外仍保持强大的抗增殖活性。在MV-4-11异种移植模型中，较高的既定剂量将肿瘤生长抑制了72.3%，并实现了代谢组学分析。这揭示了一种序贯机制：快速的MYC抑制随后是代谢酶的延迟下调，诱导血红素生物合成和NAD(+)代谢的同时紊乱。分子对接预测其可能结合UPP1、GAMT和IDO2，我们观察到MO-IPS在mRNA和蛋白质水平上下调它们的表达。关键的是，在免疫活性C1498模型中，较低的治疗相关剂量MO-IPS（20 mg/kg），经滴定以最小化直接细胞毒性，与PD-1疗法协同作用，实现了68.1%的肿瘤抑制。机制上，该组合增强了CD8(+) T细胞浸润并减少了Treg积累，导致CD8/Foxp3比值升高。这一关键发现表明，在减少暴露量下，MO-IPS的抗白血病疗效并非由明显的细胞毒性驱动，而是通过代谢重编程建立促免疫原性肿瘤微环境。总体而言，我们的工作将MO-IPS从一种细胞毒性MYC-PRMT抑制剂重新定位为一种多方面的免疫代谢治疗药物。在优化后的较低剂量下，它协调了癌症代谢脆弱性的同步破坏，并积极增强抗肿瘤免疫，为AML提供了一种精细且极具前景的组合策略。
